newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Ravva oilfield seen cash positive in 1998.
newsitem.headline: India's Ravva oilfield seen cash positive in 1998.

text.p: India's Videocon Petroleum Ltd, a unit of Videocon International Ltd, said on Friday the Ravva Offshore Oil and Gas project would have a positive cash flow by the fourth quarter of calendar 1998.

"Fiscal 1998/99 (April-March) will be our first profitable year. We expect sales of about $250 million in 1997/98, up from $96 million in 1996/97," said a senior Videocon Petroleum official, who asked not to be identified.
Videocon Petroleum holds a 25 percent equity stake in the $267 million project for drilling and producing petroleum in the Bay of Bengal, off the coast of the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
State-run oil exploration company Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) owns 40 percent, Cairn Energy Plc's Australian unit Command Petroleum Ltd owns 22.5 percent and Japan's Marubeni Corp 12.5 percent.

The Ravva field started producing petroleum in November 1996 after the consortium took it over from ONGC in January 1994. It produces between 38,000 and 39,000 barrels of crude per day, or about five percent of India's total production.
It also produces a million cubic metres of natural gas per day. All its crude and gas production is sold to the Indian government.
The official said the project would have a negative cash flow of $24.52 million for the year ending March 31, 1998.
"From 1998/99, the revenues will be constant at around $250 million until 2003, after which a fall in production will lead to falling revenues," the official said.

He said that the consortium would achieve an average net cash flow per barrel of crude of $6.62 over the 15-year life of the project. The consortium has drilled 17 oil wells, nine of which produce oil, he said.

The Ravva oilfield was assessed to have reserves of 155 million barrels of crude by U.S.-based independent petroleum services company Degolyer and MacNaughton. ONGC had estimated the reserves at 116.6 million barrels.
